direct_claims: This chart tracks deaths from earthquakes worldwide from 1500 to 2024.
It includes both direct earthquake deaths and deaths from secondary impacts such as tsunamis triggered by earthquakes.
The chart states that recent data is likely more complete than older historical estimates because of data availability limits.
The visible source line cites the National Geophysical Data Center / World Data Service (2025), and the chart is branded by Our World in Data.
Because the chart includes tsunami-related deaths triggered by earthquakes, some peaks may represent compound earthquake-tsunami disasters rather than shaking damage alone.
Historical disaster records from earlier centuries are often less complete than modern records, so comparisons between older and newer periods should be interpreted cautiously.

The note about better completeness in recent data also matters socially and politically because undercounting in older periods can distort how societies compare present-day risk with historical experience.
The time span covered is more than five centuries, from 1500 to 2024.
The visible y-axis extends to 900,000 deaths, indicating that the chart is scaled to accommodate extremely large outlier years.
The chart presents annual totals for the world rather than country-specific figures.

Because the image alone does not provide exact numeric labels for each spike, any discussion of individual peak values from this response should be treated as approximate unless confirmed by underlying metadata.
